page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-96-lssd is a general-purpose server instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The system is equipped with 372.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.88 GB per vCPU. This configuration provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, making it suitable for multi-threaded workloads that require substantial parallel processing capabilities without requiring specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.

In terms of storage and networking, this instance configuration lists local storage as none and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The absence of local storage means that persistent storage must be attached externally, which introduces a dependency on network-attached storage performance. This architectural tradeoff is typical for instances designed to prioritize centralized storage management and stateless application deployment.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c4d-standard-96-lssd is defined by its high resource density. By consolidating 96 dedicated vCPUs and 372.0 GB of RAM into a single instance, it reduces the management overhead associated with clustering multiple smaller nodes. This resource profile is suited for workloads such as large-scale web serving, enterprise application hosting, database management systems, and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
